coverage: since morning (~08:15 → ~19:40 Sun CEST; no afternoon — Sunday)
headline: Second Houthi hit on Riyadh airport as Trump still weighs joining Saudi strikes; Trump claims an energy ceasefire Zelenskyy says is news to him; Ukraine downs a third Yandex data center.

stories.title: Riyadh airport hit again; Houthis claim missiles/drones; Trump still undecided on joining Saudi strikes
facts: Material update: Sunday a projectile hit King Khalid’s Passenger Hall No 4 and sparked a fire; GACA reported injuries. Air defenses intercepted a missile nearby (BBC / Saudi coalition).

Comes a day after Saturday’s strike — deadliest on the kingdom in more than a decade. Death toll figures still circulate as 12–13 killed and ~308–309 injured; an Indian national later died of wounds (BBC).
Houthis claimed ballistic/cruise missiles and drones over 24h, also said they hit oil sites and Dammam airport, and warned airlines to stay out of Saudi airspace (except Mecca/Medina).

Airport stayed shut; Flightradar24 showed the closure extended toward midnight local Mon 12 Oct. Trump: US may join Saudi strikes — “We’ll make a decision… move very quickly.” UK’s Streeting floated more UK support.
Saudi-led coalition called Saturday’s attack a “war crime” and vowed a decisive response; Germany/Australia already warned against using Riyadh airport.
stories.whyItMatters: A same-airport follow-up strike while Washington openly debates joining Saudi operations widens Gulf escalation risk for travelers and oil routes.

stories.title: Trump announces Russia–Ukraine “energy ceasefire”; Zelenskyy: “news to me”
facts: Trump posted that an ENERGY CEASEFIRE is effective immediately and “both parties have agreed” — without detailing terms (Truth Social via Guardian).

Zelenskyy told Axios he was surprised: if Trump negotiated it with Putin, “tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready.” He earlier said any halt on Russian refinery strikes must be reciprocal with real guarantees.
No sign Russia complied Sunday: Zelenskyy said Russian drones flew “throughout the day,” with hits including Kharkiv thermal power station No 5 and more energy targets.
Row follows Friday’s US diesel-sanctions lift and Saturday’s Trump call for a “new leader” in Kyiv; Kyiv says refinery strikes continue unless Moscow stops energy hits (tagesschau / Guardian).
UK’s Burnham told Zelenskyy London will strengthen sanctions despite Washington’s diesel move; similar solidarity calls from Macron, Stubb, Carney, Tusk, von der Leyen (Guardian).
stories.whyItMatters: A White House ceasefire claim Kyiv didn’t negotiate — while Russian energy strikes continue — deepens the US–Ukraine rift just as Europe digs in behind Zelenskyy.

image.alt: Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’

stories.title: Ukraine hits a third Yandex data center; Cloud connectivity collapses
facts: Yandex said a UAV damaged its Vladimir data center east of Moscow; operations there “completely suspended,” no injuries (company Telegram / BBC).
Third strike in four days after Sasovo/Ryazan (Thu, fire; two AI supercomputers offline) and Kaluga (Fri). Yandex told users to activate disaster-recovery; remaining capacity “unstable.”
NetBlocks (via heise): Yandex connections ~80% Sunday morning; Yandex Cloud ~30%. Outages hit taxis, banking, streaming across Russia and neighbors (Astra).
Zelenskyy framed earlier DC hits as answering Russian strikes on Ukrainian data hubs (Vodafone Ukraine, Kyivstar HQ, etc.).
stories.whyItMatters: Long-range drone war is now chewing through Russia’s biggest consumer/cloud/AI stack — a civilian-facing echo of the energy infrastructure fight.
